title: Odd tori of rings compose everywhere, even tori never reach the antipode; rings of cuts separate when they bound
subject: Networks of rings joined by shared contacts, read with the canonical knot test on their space-time law
conclusion: On the n x n square torus of rule-60 rings with equally spaced law-(12,12) contacts, influence between contacts spreads by the powers of L = x + 1/x + y + 1/y = (x + y)(1 + 1/xy) over GF(2): a contact needs a ring exactly when an odd number of walks of some length k lead from one of the ring's contacts to it, first at lag g k + 1 and then at infinitely many lags. On odd tori every contact needs every ring; on even tori no contact ever needs the ring antipodal to it, and when n is a power of two the feedback is finite. Cutting the contacts round any set of rings separates it, a native separation on odd tori; one ring of cuts round the torus does not separate, and two do.
